ai.description: Nanorana vicina is a medium-sized frog reaching 6–8 cm. It is olive-brown with dark dorsal spots and a pale belly. Key features include a robust body, granular skin, and prominent, webbed toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Murree Frog (*Nanorana vicina*) is best distinguished by the presence of prominent, elongated glandular folds on its back, which are absent in similar *Nanorana* species.
ai.habitat: *Nanorana vicina* inhabits high-altitude Himalayan streams and surrounding moist forests, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Murree frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for insects along the banks of mountain streams and near rocky pools.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nanorana vicina* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon (June–August), depositing small clutches of eggs in high-altitude mountain streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nanorana vicina* is found in the Western Himalayas, ranging across northern Pakistan and the Indian states of Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand at 1,500–3,000m elevation.
ai.callDescription: The Murree Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "chirp" or "peep" calls, typically heard near fast-flowing mountain streams in its rocky, high-altitude habitat.
